content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Nathaniel Young (E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor (security DB), security training basic, recommendation read. Security says their record takes precedence - contractor with basic training, max is read.

So the two notes conflict on employment type. HR didn't look up in own database (note says "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" — actually for note 2, role was not looked up in own database, same as note 1). Employment type was looked up: contractor. Security training: basic.

The Security agent says the security record takes precedence. The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Since training is basic, max is read.

Requested write is above max, so grant max = read.

So decision: read.
